tasks.short: Coordinate product installation, testing and customer handover.

steps.what: Clarify customer deadlines, site contacts and installation requirements.
Assess site readiness, technical dependencies and required installation resources.
Agree installation and testing dates with the customer and service team.
Send booking instructions, responsibilities and agreed test requirements.
Chase delivery, access and installation milestones before the agreed dates.
Discuss test results and coordinate unresolved handover actions.

tasks.design: Configure readiness forms, dependencies and bookings in the {PROJECT} and {WORKFLOW}, linked to the {CALENDAR} and delivery milestones from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. Generate booking packs from approved templates in the {DOCS}; a service coordinator approves their release. People assess the site, negotiate dates and resolve test failures.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site conditions and competing commitments resist fixed rules. Coordination records are often scattered across calls, documents and messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and workflow features cover reminders and booking packs. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting delivery milestones and readiness checks.
tasks.still_hard: Physical readiness, contractor availability and safe testing need technical judgement. Partner status feeds may remain incomplete.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising an unsafe assumption, negotiating a workable date and preserving trust when installation slips.

ambition.what: Customer installation readiness clinic before equipment dispatch

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time chasing milestones and more time resolving readiness gaps with customers. Technical acceptance and resource allocation rights remain with the responsible service roles.

reach.learn: Delivery status codes, dispatch cutoffs and escalation routes.

reach.task: Prepare customers for site readiness reviews.
reach.learn: Installation prerequisites and the limits of commercial advice.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-10; 10-30 if national rules require employee consultation

evidence.claim: Structured readiness forms, milestone rules and booking templates can reduce coordination work; site judgement remains human.

assumptions: The representative coordinates installation; qualified service staff perform installation and testing.
The estimate covers one installation process and one delivery-status connection.
Time shares are illustrative priors for a mid-size European company.
GDPR applies to customer contacts and site records; employee consultation depends on national rules and monitoring features.
unknowns: Which role owns installation scheduling and customer handover?
Are delivery milestones and service availability accessible through supported interfaces?
Which products require site visits, certified installers or witnessed acceptance tests?
Are external service partners willing to submit structured updates?
research_questions: Which existing scheduling features support dependencies and external participants?
Which product families can use a common readiness checklist?
new_work: Maintain readiness checklists and booking templates.
Resolve overdue or contradictory milestone updates.
Monitor failed integrations and partner access.

tasks.short: Start targeted sales campaigns aligned with commercial goals and production capacity.

steps.what: Gather pipeline, account, stock and production outlook information.
Agree campaign timing and feasible volume with production and sales.
Select target accounts, offer, budget and success measures.
Write campaign messages using technical claims and the approved offer.

loop.input: Approved campaign brief, approved product claims and channel templates.
loop.output: Campaign message draft with claim references.
loop.check: Check prices and offer dates deterministically; a specialist checks claims, audience fit and wording.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per message; unresolved claims return to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover layout and fixed fields; useful technical messaging requires adapting prose to the audience.

steps.what: Check recipients, approve final messages and launch the campaign.
Review responses and capacity changes, then agree campaign adjustments.

tasks.design: Join account and pipeline data from the {CRM} with stock and capacity data from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} in a {BI} planning view. A bounded drafting loop uses approved claims from the {DOCS}; configured segments, suppression rules and approval steps in the {MARKETING_AUTOMATION} control launch. People choose the offer and interpret commercial results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Capacity and account data sit in different systems. Campaign choices depend on commercial judgement, while message preparation consumes specialist time.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing campaign tools already support segmentation, suppression and scheduling. Faster integration development and bounded drafting reduce preparation costs without needing autonomous campaign control.
tasks.still_hard: Production forecasts change, customer response is uncertain and campaign attribution is imperfect. Technical claims and channel permissions need reliable source records.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a credible offer, understanding customer priorities and balancing demand against delivery promises.
tasks.altitude: The representative can spend more time testing offers with selected accounts and interpreting responses. With delegated limits, they can adjust audience and timing within an approved budget; broader pricing rights require explicit delegation.

reach.task: Balance campaign demand against margin and available capacity.
reach.learn: Contribution margin, forecast uncertainty and experiment design.

reach.task: Design follow-up offers around installation or maintenance needs.
reach.learn: Service capacity, attachment opportunities and customer lifecycle signals.

build_days.consent_and_access: 4-12; 10-30 if national rules require employee consultation

evidence.claim: Deterministic joins, segments and launch rules can support campaign preparation; commercial choices remain judgement work.
Sales software supports lead research, qualification and outreach today; this does not establish autonomous campaign planning.
In the Netherlands, seller-observation features can require works council consent; national requirements vary.

assumptions: The campaign targets business buyers of technical or scientific goods.
The estimate covers one campaign channel and existing customer and product records.
Time shares are illustrative and include cross-functional work.
GDPR and applicable national marketing rules govern contact use; channel permissions are checked before launch.
No employee scoring or call analytics is required for the proposed design.
unknowns: Who approves offers, technical claims and campaign spending?
How current and granular is the production forecast?
Are contact permissions and objections recorded consistently?
Which audience and timing changes can the representative approve?
research_questions: Which segmentation and approval features are already available in the existing systems?
Which campaign outcome measures distinguish new demand from purchases that would happen anyway?
new_work: Review generated messages and claim references.
Maintain segment definitions, suppressions and capacity thresholds.
Investigate stale forecasts and failed data refreshes.
Evaluate campaign results and record adjustment decisions.

tasks.short: Check materials lists against customer requirements, product records and compatibility rules.

steps.what: Locate the latest materials list, drawings and customer requirements.
Transcribe document lines into a comparison sheet.

loop.input: Document materials lists; structured lists bypass the model.
loop.output: Item references, quantities, units and revision identifiers with source locations.
loop.check: Validate schema, line counts, quantities, units and exact item matches; review ambiguous or unreadable fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry per document; unresolved lines return to manual transcription.
loop.why_not_simpler: Variable document layouts need interpretation; structured imports and fixed templates use deterministic parsing.

steps.what: Compare item codes, quantities, units, revisions and required accessories.
Resolve unclear specifications, substitutions and compatibility exceptions.
Record the checked list and send its revision reference to order processing.

tasks.design: Link revision-controlled lists in the {DOCS} to item and configuration records in the {ERP}, then run deterministic completeness and compatibility checks. A bounded extraction loop handles variable document lists; ambiguous fields and technical exceptions go to people. The {WORKFLOW} records the verified revision and passes it to order processing only after required corrections are approved.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer documents vary, revision links are weak and compatibility knowledge is partly undocumented. Manual comparisons bridge documents and product records.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can now be bounded by line-level checks. Faster coding makes item matching, unit validation and revision tracking cheaper to connect.
tasks.still_hard: A valid item code does not prove technical suitability. Missing design context, undocumented dependencies and complex drawings still need engineering review.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising technically plausible but unsuitable combinations and clarifying what the customer actually intends to build.

ambition.what: Customer materials preflight report before quotation

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time copying and comparing lists and more time resolving requirements before quotation. They can explain documented discrepancies; approval of technical substitutions remains with the sales engineer.

reach.task: Investigate materials compatibility and substitution exceptions.
reach.learn: Revision control, engineering units and product dependency rules.

reach.task: Release orders against the verified materials revision.
reach.learn: Item master conventions and change-control checkpoints.

evidence.claim: Configurators connected to commercial systems support product selection and rule-driven configuration today.
Document extraction followed by item-master checks is available for order intake; materials verification requires additional engineering rules.
Revision, unit and accessory checks can be deterministic when approved product rules are available.

assumptions: Some materials lists arrive as documents and are manually copied into comparison sheets.
The estimate covers one product family and accessible item records; extensive rule discovery adds work.
The workflow blocks completion while extraction fields or required technical approvals remain unresolved.
GDPR applies where documents contain personal data; customer technical documents also require controlled access.
unknowns: What share of lists is structured, document-based or embedded in drawings?
Are authoritative revisions identifiable without asking the customer?
Which compatibility rules already exist in the current systems?
Who may approve substitutions and release the verified list?
research_questions: Which checks can reuse existing configuration rules?
Which document layouts and engineering notation cause extraction failures?
new_work: Maintain unit mappings, accessory dependencies and revision rules.
Resolve exceptions with engineering and customers.
Sample completed checks and investigate missed discrepancies.

tasks.short: Verify business customer credit information and route credit exceptions to finance.

steps.what: Retrieve the customer rating from the {OTHER} credit-reference service.
Check receivables, payment history, open orders and existing credit limits.
Compare rating freshness and customer exposure with credit policy.
Resolve exceptions and approve the credit disposition.
Record the approved status and tell order processing about restrictions.

tasks.design: Connect the {OTHER} credit-reference service to customer identities and exposure records in the {ERP}. Configure freshness, exposure and policy checks, with the credit manager approving the disposition before any limit or restriction changes. Synchronise the approved status and review date to the {CRM}; no model is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: External ratings and internal exposure are separated, and customer identity matching can be unreliable. Available credit features may not have been configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Supported data feeds and existing credit modules cover much of the work. Faster integration development reduces the cost of joining identities, reports and approval records.
tasks.still_hard: Ratings can lag events, group structures complicate exposure and commercial pressure can distort exceptions. Access to credit data may require paid licences.
tasks.human_edge: Interpreting conflicting evidence and negotiating workable payment terms without hiding financial risk.

ambition.what: Event-triggered credit reviews before unusually large orders

tasks.altitude: The representative receives a current credit status with fewer manual checks and can discuss feasible payment options earlier. Finance retains credit-limit and override authority; the representative gains no credit approval rights.

reach.task: Handle held orders using approved credit restrictions.
reach.learn: Exposure calculations, release conditions and escalation routes.

reach.task: Evaluate commercial alternatives for credit-constrained accounts.
reach.learn: Payment security, margin tradeoffs and credit policy boundaries.

evidence.claim: Business credit verification can use deterministic identity, freshness and exposure checks without a model.
Assessing natural persons' creditworthiness is an EU AI Act classification question distinct from ordinary business-record checks.

assumptions: The task concerns trade credit for incorporated business customers.
Finance owns credit decisions; the representative gathers information and communicates approved status.
The estimate covers one credit-data provider and existing customer identity records.
GDPR applies to personal data in reports; sole traders, guarantors and natural-person credit decisions need separate assessment.
No model-based credit scoring or solely automated adverse decision is introduced.
unknowns: Which credit-data subscriptions and interfaces are available?
How reliably do customer records identify legal entities and corporate groups?
Are existing credit and approval features enabled in the current systems?
Does the customer base include sole traders or personal guarantees?
Which roles can view reports, approve limits and release held orders?
research_questions: Which supported feeds provide rating changes and report timestamps?
Which exposure calculations and approval controls can be configured without custom code?
new_work: Resolve legal-entity mismatches and stale reports.
Maintain policy thresholds and approval permissions.
Review exceptions and record reasons for overrides.
Monitor feed failures, licensing and credit-status synchronisation.

role.altitude: The representative spends less time assembling records, checking routine fields and chasing updates. More of the week goes to technical discovery, delivery commitments and commercial choices; engineering acceptance, campaign spending and credit overrides remain with their authorised roles unless explicitly delegated.
reach: Sales engineer: investigate technical requirements and compatibility exceptions.
Order clerk: connect verified materials, credit status and dispatch readiness.
Sales manager: propose capacity-aware offers and interpret campaign results.
skills_to_grow: Technical requirement discovery and revision control
Campaign experiment design and margin analysis
role.ambitious_version: Offer a coordinated pre-order review covering materials, installation readiness and payment feasibility, with technical and financial decisions approved by the responsible specialists.
